knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=\frac{4\pi}{9}$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{3\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} &=\frac{3}{2}\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=\frac{3}{2}\frac{\sin(2x)}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=\frac{3}{2}\tan(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

The denominator is nonzero, and $\tan(2x)=\sin(2x)/\cos(2x)$.

Substitute $x=\frac{4\pi}{9}$ and double the whole angle: $2x=\frac{8\pi}{9}$. The result is

$$
\frac{3}{2}\tan\left(\frac{8\pi}{9}\right) .
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=34^\circ$. Expand the square and combine the squared terms.

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\sin x+\cos x)^2 &=\sin^2 x+2\sin x\cos x+\cos^2 x \\ &=1+2\sin x\cos x \\ &=1+\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x=1$ and $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$. Multiply both terms by $3$.

Substitute $x=34^\circ$ and double the whole angle: $2x=68^\circ$. The result is

$$
3+3\sin\left(68^\circ\right) .
$$

knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=13^\circ$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\sin x\cos x}{2\cos(2x)} &=\frac{1}{4}\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=\frac{1}{4}\frac{\sin(2x)}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=\frac{1}{4}\tan(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

The denominator is nonzero, and $\tan(2x)=\sin(2x)/\cos(2x)$.

Substitute $x=13^\circ$ and double the whole angle: $2x=26^\circ$. The result is

$$
\frac{1}{4}\tan\left(26^\circ\right) .
$$

knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=37^\circ$. Expand the square and combine the squared terms.

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\sin x-\cos x)^2 &=\sin^2 x-2\sin x\cos x+\cos^2 x \\ &=1-2\sin x\cos x \\ &=1-\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x=1$ and $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$. Multiply both terms by $3$.

Substitute $x=37^\circ$ and double the whole angle: $2x=74^\circ$. The result is

$$
3-3\sin\left(74^\circ\right) .
$$
